opportunities.title: Branch Art Exhibit: Works by Animative Space, Back To The Essence
opportunities.description: Throughout the month of November, the works by Animative Space are on display at Albion Branch. Animative Space is a Toronto based multimedia art studio where our mantra is, “We create stylized art”. Our chosen art form allows us to blend both physical and digital products; paintings, designer toys, stickers, murals and nfts into vibrant styles of art that pushes the boundaries of creativity. "The inspiration for our work comes from artists of the past as to build a future you must know your past. Other art avenues that play a huge inspiration in what we create are anime, street art, graffiti." The exhibit can be viewed during Albion branch's open hours. Please check the Albion branch page before you visit. Free. All are welcome. Photo credit: Animativespace, Stephan Spencer, Essence of Peace, Pencil, Medium

opportunities.title: Python Essentials 1 Learning Circle
opportunities.description: Learn Python and build your programming skills in a supportive group. This learning circle will meet on Monday evenings from November 2 to December 7, 4-6pm. Learning circles are study groups guided by staff for people who want to take a free online course together in a welcoming space. Learners meet weekly and work together through the course materials. Participants are expected to commit to the duration of the course and attend all learning circle sessions. Used by startups and tech giants like Google, Facebook, Netflix, and more, Python offers you endless possibilities for creating small and large-scale software projects. User-friendly with easy-to-read code, Python is a great first programming language to learn and requires no prior programming knowledge. Python skills open you up to careers in almost any industry and are required if you want to continue to more advanced, higher paying software development and engineering roles such as software engineer, systems administrator, and security engineer. Python Essentials 1 In this course, you will learn in-demand skills such as how to design, develop, and improve computer programs, methods for analyzing problems using programming, programming best practices, and more. The course also prepares you for the PCEP – Certified Entry-Level Python Programmer certification (Exam PCEP-30-0x). For more information about the Python learning circle, please contact networkingacademy@tpl.ca Information Collection Notice: The personal information on this form is collected by the Toronto Public Library under the Public Libraries Act, sections 20(a), 20(c), and 20(d). opportunities.title: Five Pieces of the AI Puzzle
opportunities.description: This interactive 60-minute session demystifies artificial intelligence through a unique five-piece puzzle framework, guiding participants to better understand AI’s presence, challenge common perceptions, and actively shape how they live and work alongside it. Combining multimedia, collaboration, and real-world examples, the program empowers audiences to move beyond passive awareness toward confident, informed engagement with AI. This is a multi-media presentation with video clips, props, group discussion and begins with an opening Puzzle Pieces song and an actual solve a 5-piece puzzle challenge ice breaker. opportunities.title: Data Analytics Essentials Learning Circle
opportunities.description: Interested in learning about data analytics? Let's take a free online course together in a welcoming space! A learning circle is a study group, guided by library staff, for people who want to take a free online course together in a supportive and welcoming environment. Organizations all over the world recognize the value of analytics. Together, we'll learn about the essential tools used in this field. In this 12-week learning circle, we will work through the Data Analytics Essentials course from Cisco Networking Academy. We will explore the fundamental tools of a data analyst, including how to: transform, organize and visualize data with spreadsheet tools like Excel query data from a relational database using SQL improve data presentations using business intelligence tools like Tableau We will meet weekly, in-person, every Tuesday afternoon, September 15 - December 8, 2-3:30 PM (12 sessions). Participants are expected to commit to the duration of the course and attend sessions on a weekly basis. Learners who complete the course will be able to: earn a digital badge download a certificate of completion

opportunities.title: Python Essentials 1 and 2 Learning Circle
opportunities.description: Learn Python and build your programming skills in a supportive group. This learning circle will meet on Tuesday afternoons from September 22 to December 8, 2-3:30pm. Learning circles are study groups guided by staff for people who want to take a free online course together in a welcoming space. Learners meet weekly and work together through the course materials. Participants are expected to commit to the duration of the course and attend all learning circle sessions. Learners who successfully complete both courses will earn a digital badge and certificate of completion. Python Essentials 1 is the first in a 2-course series that teaches computer programming skills including how to design, develop, and improve computer programs using the Python programming language. The course covers essential programming topics such as data types, variables, control flow, functions, and exceptions. Python Essentials 2 is the second in a 2-course series that will prepare you for the PCAP – Certified Associate in Python Programming certification exam at Pearson VUE. This intermediate-level course covers advanced aspects of Python programming, including modules, packages, exceptions, file processing and object-oriented programming (OOP). opportunities.title: 3D Design with Onshape
opportunities.description: Learn how to create parametric designs using cloud based software Onshape. This hands-on workshop introduces participants to the fundamentals of 3D design using Onshape, a cloud-based CAD software. Whether you're an aspiring engineer, designer, or hobbyist, this session provides the tools and knowledge to start creating your own 3D models. What You’ll Learn: Getting Started: Overview of Onshape's interface, navigation tools, and cloud-based collaboration features. Core Design Principles: Understanding 3D modeling basics, including sketches, extrusions, and revolutions. Hands-On Practice: Creating simple 3D parts, assembling components, and exploring design modifications. Best Practices: Tips for efficient modeling, managing design iterations, and exporting models for 3D printing or other applications. This program is ideal for beginners with no prior experience in CAD software, as well as those looking to explore Onshape's capabilities. Registration will start 2 weeks before this class. Computers will be provided. opportunities.title: 3D Design with Onshape
opportunities.description: Learn how to create parametric designs using cloud based software Onshape. This hands-on workshop introduces participants to the fundamentals of 3D design using Onshape, a cloud-based CAD software. Whether you're an aspiring engineer, designer, or hobbyist, this session provides the tools and knowledge to start creating your own 3D models. What You’ll Learn: Getting Started: Overview of Onshape's interface, navigation tools, and cloud-based collaboration features. Core Design Principles: Understanding 3D modeling basics, including sketches, extrusions, and revolutions. Hands-On Practice: Creating simple 3D parts, assembling components, and exploring design modifications. Best Practices: Tips for efficient modeling, managing design iterations, and exporting models for 3D printing or other applications. This program is ideal for beginners with no prior experience in CAD software, as well as those looking to explore Onshape's capabilities. Registration will start 2 weeks before this class. opportunities.title: Computers for Beginners
opportunities.description: Computers for Beginners 1: Use the Mouse A class on how to use a mouse for absolute beginners with little or no computer experience. In this first session you will: Observe and practice how to operate a mouse effectively Understand various mouse pointers and cursors Review basic keyboard functions Use the mouse for basic Windows functions Upon completion of this class students will be able to use a computer mouse at a basic level and will be able to go online for additional practice. Computers for Beginners 2: Use the Keyboard A class on basic keyboard functions for absolute beginners with little or no computer experience. In this second session you will: Familiarize yourself through practice with the most essential keyboard functions (alphabet, number and symbol keys) Practice proper keyboarding posture Upon completion of this class students will be able to use a keyboard at a beginner level and know how to go online for additional practice. Computers for Beginners 3: Use the Internet An introductory class on the Internet for absolute beginners with little computer experience. In this fourth session you will: Understand how to read a web site address Practice using web addresses Search for information using a search engine Explore a web site in detail to understand its key components Upon completion of this class students will be able to use the internet at a beginner level and complete simple searches. Computers for Beginners 4: Use Google Search and Maps A class on using Google's filters, tools, and Maps for absolute beginners with little computer experience. In this fifth session you will: Use Google search tools more effectively to find websites, images, and news sites Explore Google Maps to find addresses and get directions for transit and road travel. Upon completion of this class students will be able to use more advanced search engine features and use Google Maps at a basic level. Computers for Beginners 5: Use Windows A class on essential basic Windows skills for absolute beginners with little computer experience. In this third session you will: Become familiar with the Windows (10) operating system Practice using common Windows features: File Explorer, Desktop, Taskbar, Windows, Applications Upon completion of this class students will have a basic understanding of how to create and organize files in the Windows environment.

opportunities.description: Python is an open source programming language that is used for creating web applications, web content, mathematics and system scripting. In this second Python session we will leverage everything we learned about loops and blocks in part one to create our very own functions. We'll take a look at how to approach function design, how to allow users to enter data into functions through arguments, and how to get our functions to return results. opportunities.description: AI technologies have become increasingly prevalent in many aspects of modern life, including healthcare, finance, transportation, and entertainment. Some examples of AI applications include virtual assistants like Siri and Alexa, self-driving cars, fraud detection systems, and personalized recommendations in online shopping. Come join this beginner in-person class to learn what AI is, how it learns and predicts outcomes, considerations when using GenAI applications, and how the Internet of Things (IOT) applies to AI. For ages 13+. Drop-in, no registration required.

opportunities.title: Modern Careers: Unlocking New AI Career Paths
opportunities.description: Join one of TPL's Career Coaches in Residence, Sangeetha Dikshit and guest speaker Bhumika Arora for this interactive discussion. Artificial intelligence is changing more than just how software gets built. It is creating brand new ways to work across every industry. From tech roles evolving with AI tools to flexible remote gigs and new opportunities in non-technical fields, AI offers unique options for early-career professionals and students entering the workforce. Join our guest speaker Bhumika Arora in this interactive session that helps you understand the current AI job landscape and build a clear strategy for your future. Sangeetha Dikshit is one of TPL's Career Coaches in Residence and is a Career and Leadership Coach empowering individuals to navigate career transitions, develop in-demand skills, and achieve professional success. Bhumika Arora is a Career & Business Coach and AI Transformation Advisor. Bhumika works with individuals pursuing transitions into tech and customer success roles. Bhumika also collaborates with AI‑centric organizations as an Advisory Partner, contributing to initiatives related to emerging technologies and workforce development. This program is part of TPL's Career Coaches in Residence and is generously supported by our lead donor Azrieli Foundation along with supporting donors Fidelity Canada, Friends of Toronto Public Library, South Chapter and The William and Nona Heaslip Foundation. For more information, please visit tpl.ca/careercoach

opportunities.title: Bridging Minds: Supporting Mental Health in the Early Years (0–5) — Small Actions, Big Impact
opportunities.description: Dr. Aliza Israel and Dr. Tatiana Valverde, child psychiatrists at Women’s College Hospital, will explore why the early years of life are so important for children's mental health, emotional well-being, and development. From birth to age five, children begin to develop the foundations for relationships, emotional regulation, learning, and resilience. Through everyday interactions, play, and nurturing relationships, parents, caregivers, and communities can help create a strong foundation for lifelong well-being. What to Expect: Understanding Early Childhood: Why the first five years are an important period for brain development, emotional growth, and lifelong mental health The Power of Relationships: How responsive caregiving, secure relationships, play, and everyday interactions help young children feel safe, connected, and supported Supporting Big Feelings: Understanding co-regulation and how parents and caregivers can help young children navigate big emotions, manage frustration, and gradually develop their own emotional regulation skills Small Actions, Lasting Impact: Practical, everyday ways families, caregivers, and communities can support children's mental health and help give every child a healthy start About the Presenters: Dr. Aliza Israel is a child and adolescent psychiatrist at Women's College Hospital, and lecturer at the University of Toronto in child psychiatry and women's mental health. Her work focuses on the interplay between maternal and child mental health, and in promoting resilience in young families. Dr. Israel lives in Toronto, Canada, with her husband and three rapidly-growing boys. She is also an amateur juggler who may or may not secretly wish to run away with the circus. Dr. Tatiana Valverde da Conceicao is a Child and Adolescent Psychiatrist at the Reproductive Life Stages Program at Women’s College Hospital. She’s an Assistant Professor at University of Toronto. Her clinical work involves general Child and Adolescent Psychiatry with a special focus on Early Childhood Mental Health. In addition to her clinical and academic work, the experience of being a mother influences and enriches her professional perspective. About the Series Bridging Minds: Health & Science Conversations is a partnership between the Toronto Public Library and Women’s College Hospital. Through monthly discussions led by experts from across different clinical areas and scientific disciplines, this series provides attendees with the opportunity to engage directly with our topics and speakers and empowers communities to navigate health and science topics confidently, inspiring a future of informed decision-making. Learn more: https://www.womenscollegehospital.ca/bridging-minds/ Reserve Your Spot Today! This virtual Zoom event is free to join but registration is required. Once registered, you’ll receive an email with the Zoom link. We can’t wait to see you there!

opportunities.title: Resilience Reads: a climate neighbourhood reading party
opportunities.description: Join us to share the joy of reading, while building climate resilience knowledge. Members are invited to discuss a book they are reading, tell stories, and empower each other to explore community-driven solutions. Each party will start with a quiet read and reflect time, with opportunities to join group discussions later on over refreshments. APRIL 15-Learning from trees for Earth Month The Overstory by Richard Power MAY 20-All women are water defenders Memory of Water by Emmi Itaranta or your favourite book featuring water! JUNE 17– Righting our relationship with land Earth Keeper by N. Scott Momaday or your favourite book that shares how words are medicine! JULY 15– Climate migration or the borders between us are not lines that divide us, but seams that connect us Gun Island / The Hungry Tide by Amitav Ghosh or your favourite island setting summer read! Copies are available in the branch to pick up, while supplies last. AUGUST 19--Fossil Fuel Folly American War by Omar El Akkad or your favourite dystopian read! SEPTEMBER 16--We Need Pollinators The History of Bees by Maja Lunde or your favourite animal-centred book! OCTOBER 21--Climate Change is Scary The Annual Migration of Clouds by Premee Mohamed or a different book that shares a scary future ecological crisis! NOVEMBER 18--Climate changes everything The Ministry for the Future by Kim Stanley Robinson or your favourite time travel read! A learning circle is a study group, guided by library staff, for people who want to take a free online course together in a supportive and welcoming environment. We will explore the fundamental tools of a data analyst, including how to: transform, organize and visualize data with spreadsheet tools like Excel query data from a relational database using SQL improve data presentations using business intelligence tools like Tableau We will meet online every Thursday evening, September 24 - December 10, 6-7:30 PM (12 sessions). opportunities.title: Computers for Beginners
opportunities.description: Computers for Beginners 1: Use the Mouse A class on how to use a mouse for absolute beginners with little or no computer experience. In this first session you will: Observe and practice how to operate a mouse effectively Understand various mouse pointers and cursors Review basic keyboard functions Use the mouse for basic Windows functions Upon completion of this class students will be able to use a computer mouse at a basic level and will be able to go online for additional practice. Computers for Beginners 2: Use the Keyboard A class on basic keyboard functions for absolute beginners with little or no computer experience. In this second session you will: Familiarize yourself through practice with the most essential keyboard functions (alphabet, number and symbol keys) Practice proper keyboarding posture Upon completion of this class students will be able to use a keyboard at a beginner level and know how to go online for additional practice. Computers for Beginners 3: Use the Internet An introductory class on the Internet for absolute beginners with little computer experience. In this fourth session you will: Understand how to read a web site address Practice using web addresses Search for information using a search engine Explore a web site in detail to understand its key components Upon completion of this class students will be able to use the internet at a beginner level and complete simple searches. Computers for Beginners 4: Use Google Search and Maps A class on using Google's filters, tools, and Maps for absolute beginners with little computer experience. In this fifth session you will: Use Google search tools more effectively to find websites, images, and news sites Explore Google Maps to find addresses and get directions for transit and road travel. Upon completion of this class students will be able to use more advanced search engine features and use Google Maps at a basic level. Computers for Beginners 5: Use Windows A class on essential basic Windows skills for absolute beginners with little computer experience. In this third session you will: Become familiar with the Windows (10) operating system Practice using common Windows features: File Explorer, Desktop, Taskbar, Windows, Applications Upon completion of this class students will have a basic understanding of how to create and organize files in the Windows environment.

opportunities.title: Who Should Own AI? Building Public AI
opportunities.description: If AI becomes as important as roads, electricity, or libraries, who should own it? Who decides what it's used for? Who gets access and to say no? This panel discussion, as part of our Innovator-in-Residence program with Ryan Kelln , will include speakers building public-interest AI, working in civic tech, and organizing communities affected by AI decisions. We'll explore what's already being built, from open models and public compute to community-owned data, and what's being privatized. You'll get to draft your own "public AI requirements" and see what others think should be guaranteed to everyone. The future of AI is being decided now; this is a chance to have a say in it. Featuring: Alex Olson , Director of University of Toronto’s Centre for Analytics & AI Engineering Khasir Hean , Founder of Technologists for Democracy, Machine Learning engineer Nathalie Claire DiBerardino , Project Lead, DARO Registration is required and will start October 9, 2026 at 12:30 PM. Note: Your spot will not be guaranteed after 5 minutes of the start of the program. After this time, remaining seats will be filled on a first come, first serve basis until capacity is reached. opportunities.title: Python Essentials 1 Learning Circle
opportunities.description: Learn Python and build your programming skills in a supportive group. This learning circle will meet on Monday evenings from November 2 to December 7, 4-6pm. Learning circles are study groups guided by staff for people who want to take a free online course together in a welcoming space. Learners meet weekly and work together through the course materials. Participants are expected to commit to the duration of the course and attend all learning circle sessions. Used by startups and tech giants like Google, Facebook, Netflix, and more, Python offers you endless possibilities for creating small and large-scale software projects. User-friendly with easy-to-read code, Python is a great first programming language to learn and requires no prior programming knowledge. Python skills open you up to careers in almost any industry and are required if you want to continue to more advanced, higher paying software development and engineering roles such as software engineer, systems administrator, and security engineer. Python Essentials 1 In this course, you will learn in-demand skills such as how to design, develop, and improve computer programs, methods for analyzing problems using programming, programming best practices, and more. The course also prepares you for the PCEP – Certified Entry-Level Python Programmer certification (Exam PCEP-30-0x). opportunities.title: Bee-ing a Pollinator Protector: Plan Now for a Buzzing Spring Garden
opportunities.description: Saving the bees is an environmental cause that resonates deeply with Canadians. While most of us might not be thinking about bees this time of year, our actions during the colder months can still support these pollinators, particularly native bees, which are crucial and threatened by climate change, habitat loss, and other pressures. In honour of the late bee scientist Sheila Colla, this presentation will offer practical tips on planting and maintaining gardens that provide beautifully blooming habitat for pollinators, with a particular focus on how native plants support wild bees. Presented by Lorraine Johnson , who co-authored A Garden for the Rusty-Patched Bumblebee with Sheila Colla, as part of TPL's environmental program series, Our Fragile Planet , supported by Friends of Toronto Public Library, South Chapter.​ Free. Register for a reminder. Doors open at 6:30 pm for attendees to mingle, chat with Lorraine, and explore related resources. Presentation begins at 7:00 pm. Place a hold or borrow from Toronto Public Library: A Garden for the Rusty-patched Bumblebee (book) A Garden for the Rusty-Patched Bumblebee (ebook) This program will also be offered virtually on Tuesday, November 3, 2026 , from 7:00 pm to 8:00 pm, as part of Climate Action Week. To register for the online program and for more info, see the listing . opportunities.title: From Screen Addiction to Self-Motivation: Ending the Daily Battle Over Video Games and Phones (**in Cantonese/Mandarin)
opportunities.description: Are daily struggles over gaming and phone use turning your home into a battleground? Do you feel caught between wanting high achievements for your children and feeling helpless against the pull of modern technology? You are not alone. In today’s digital age, traditional discipline methods often lead to constant power struggles, tears, and frustration for both parents and kids. Join Hopewoods Psychotherapy and Sparkling Seeds for a transformational, 1-hour parent workshop designed specifically for Chinese-speaking families navigating the digital world. What You Will Learn The Brain Behind the Screen (Neuroscience): Discover how dopamine and gaming design impact your child’s developing brain, and why simple restrictions or lectures often backfire. Connection Before Direction: Learn how to engage your child’s "upstairs brain" to manage emotional meltdowns and shift from conflict to co-regulation. Bridging Tradition and Attachment: Honour traditional parenting goals for discipline and success while deepening secure attachment and emotional trust. Fostering Self-Motivation: Transition from constant nagging and enforcement to helping your child cultivate intrinsic motivation and healthy self-control. __________________ Please note this workshop will be presented in Cantonese/Mandarin: 從螢幕成癮到自主動力 告別每日電玩與手機的拉鋸戰 每天為了手機和電子遊戲與孩子展開「攻防戰」，讓家裡變成戰場嗎？既希望孩子學業有成、有自律能力，又對無處不在的電子產品感到無力與焦慮？ 你並不孤單。在數位時代，傳統的強迫與管教方式往往只會引發不斷的權力鬥爭、眼淚與親子關係的撕裂。 誠邀您參加由 Hopewoods Psychotherapy 與 Sparkling Seeds 舉辦的 1 小時家長專題工作坊，專為華人家庭量身打造，帶您以全新的科學與心理學視角解開科技困局。 工作坊重點內容 螢幕背後的大腦機制（腦科學視角）： 了解多巴胺與遊戲機制如何影響孩子發育中的大腦，以及為什麼單純的強行禁止或說教往往適得其反。 先連結，後引導： 學習如何引導孩子的「上層大腦」，應對情緒失控，將親子衝突轉化為共同調節。 融合傳統期望與依附理論： 在尊重華人家庭對紀律與成就期望的同時，建立深層的安全依附與信任關係。 激發內在學習動力： 告別每日嘮叨與強迫，幫助孩子建立內在動機與健康的自我管理能力。 "當我們理解科技對大腦的影響，並以『依附關係』為導向時，我們不只是在減少螢幕使用時間，更是重塑與孩子終身受用的親子信任。"

opportunities.title: Journée pédagogique: Explorum - Bombes à bain
opportunities.description: L’expérience des bombes à bain est une expérience simple qui illustre une des réactions chimiques les plus communes : la neutralisation acidobasique qui forme un sel et de l'eau. Cette activité relaxante permet aux enfants de faire leur propre bombe à bain et de comprendre que cette réaction produit du gaz (des bulles) ; ils apprennent que l’acide contient du cations H+ et que la base contient des anions OH- qui réagissent ensemble pour former du sel et de l'eau. Chaque participant combine ses ingrédients et confectionne sa propre bombe à bain qu’il emporte avec lui emballée dans un petit sac en cellophane. The bath bomb experience is a simple activity that illustrates one of the most common chemical reactions: acid-base neutralization, which forms a salt and water. This relaxing activity allows children to create their own bath bomb and understand that this reaction produces gas (bubbles). They learn that the acid contains H+ ions and the base contains OH- ions, which react together to form salt and water. Each participant combines their ingredients and crafts their own bath bomb to take home, packaged in a small cellophane bag. Accessibilité: Le sous-titrage en direct ou automatique, l’interprétation en langue des signes, les services d’intervenant, ou les services d’accompagnement sont disponibles sur demande. opportunities.title: Computers for Beginners
opportunities.description: Computers for Beginners 1: Use the Mouse A class on how to use a mouse for absolute beginners with little or no computer experience. In this first session you will: Observe and practice how to operate a mouse effectively Understand various mouse pointers and cursors Review basic keyboard functions Use the mouse for basic Windows functions Upon completion of this class students will be able to use a computer mouse at a basic level and will be able to go online for additional practice. Computers for Beginners 2: Use the Keyboard A class on basic keyboard functions for absolute beginners with little or no computer experience. In this second session you will: Familiarize yourself through practice with the most essential keyboard functions (alphabet, number and symbol keys) Practice proper keyboarding posture Upon completion of this class students will be able to use a keyboard at a beginner level and know how to go online for additional practice. Computers for Beginners 3: Use the Internet An introductory class on the Internet for absolute beginners with little computer experience. In this fourth session you will: Understand how to read a web site address Practice using web addresses Search for information using a search engine Explore a web site in detail to understand its key components Upon completion of this class students will be able to use the internet at a beginner level and complete simple searches. Computers for Beginners 4: Use Google Search and Maps A class on using Google's filters, tools, and Maps for absolute beginners with little computer experience. In this fifth session you will: Use Google search tools more effectively to find websites, images, and news sites Explore Google Maps to find addresses and get directions for transit and road travel. Upon completion of this class students will be able to use more advanced search engine features and use Google Maps at a basic level. Computers for Beginners 5: Use Windows A class on essential basic Windows skills for absolute beginners with little computer experience. In this third session you will: Become familiar with the Windows (10) operating system Practice using common Windows features: File Explorer, Desktop, Taskbar, Windows, Applications Upon completion of this class students will have a basic understanding of how to create and organize files in the Windows environment.

opportunities.description: Are you a homeschooler family? Markham Public Library hosts weekly meetups for homeschooler families on Monday mornings at the Angus Glen Library Branch from 10:30AM - 12:00PM . These meetups give participating caregivers and children an opportunity to connect with other homeschooling families, work together to explore various STEAM building and literacy development focused activities, learn about library resources, meet special guest speakers, and more! Introduction to Piano! Let's explore music as Teleki Music provides students with an introduction to piano/keyboard basics. PLEASE NOTE: Adults (caregivers) are responsible for supervising and assisting the children in their care with all planned activities and/or exercises Most planned activities are suitable for ages 5+ and may be subject to change Active participation and engagement of all caregivers is required ⚠️ PLEASE REGISTER TO ATTEND: We require advance registration for this program due to limited space, room capacity, and to support the library in our ability to plan activities and prepare supplies. We ask that all participants (caregivers and children) please sign-up for each session to guarantee your spot! *** ***For example, if there is 1 caregiver and 3 children attending, please indicate 4 in the registration.

opportunities.title: Python Essentials 1 Learning Circle
opportunities.description: Learn Python and build your programming skills in a supportive group. This learning circle will meet on Monday evenings from November 2 to December 7, 4-6pm. Learning circles are study groups guided by staff for people who want to take a free online course together in a welcoming space. Learners meet weekly and work together through the course materials. Participants are expected to commit to the duration of the course and attend all learning circle sessions. Used by startups and tech giants like Google, Facebook, Netflix, and more, Python offers you endless possibilities for creating small and large-scale software projects. User-friendly with easy-to-read code, Python is a great first programming language to learn and requires no prior programming knowledge. Python skills open you up to careers in almost any industry and are required if you want to continue to more advanced, higher paying software development and engineering roles such as software engineer, systems administrator, and security engineer. Python Essentials 1 In this course, you will learn in-demand skills such as how to design, develop, and improve computer programs, methods for analyzing problems using programming, programming best practices, and more. The course also prepares you for the PCEP – Certified Entry-Level Python Programmer certification (Exam PCEP-30-0x). opportunities.description: Ready to develop the skills to use generative AI (GenAI) tools effectively and responsibly for work and daily life? Join our staff-facilitated Learning Circle to complete the self-paced Google Prompting specialization. By completing this Learning Circle program, you will earn a Google Prompting Essentials certificate to share on your resume, LinkedIn and social media profiles! What You'll Learn This program is designed for those with some experience with using GenAI. Through short videos, articles, assignments and quizzes, you will discover: Essential Prompting Skills : How to use a prompting framework to create a desired output with GenAI; how to evaluate and refine your results. Everyday Work Tasks: Strategies to draft content, brainstorm ideas, create tables, timelines, and more. Data & Presentations: How to explore data visualization and use GenAI responsibly when working with data. Advanced Techniques: How to use prompt chaining for complex tasks and prompt versioning to save and reuse your best prompts over time. Learning Circles are study groups guided by library staff for people who want to complete the Google Prompting specialization together in a welcoming space: Learners meet weekly and work together through course materials. Participants are expected to commit to attending all four Learning Circle sessions. Some Experience with GenAI Recommended: This course is ideal for participants who have completed the AI Essentials course Learning Circle. How to Joi n a Learning Circle: Register once for the first session of this event series, in order to attend all sessions. Please sign up with a valid email address. A valid TPL library card is required for online circles. Attend all four sessions online via Zoom, on Tuesdays December 1, 8, 15 from 1:30-4:30pm. Registration is a two-step process. First, participants must complete their registration through this page. After this step, library staff will follow up to request additional information in order to complete the registration. opportunities.description: Interested in learning about data analytics? Let's take a free online course together in a welcoming space! A learning circle is a study group, guided by library staff, for people who want to take a free online course together in a supportive and welcoming environment. Organizations all over the world recognize the value of analytics. Together, we'll learn about the essential tools used in this field. In this 12-week learning circle, we will work through the Data Analytics Essentials course from Cisco Networking Academy. We will explore the fundamental tools of a data analyst, including how to: transform, organize and visualize data with spreadsheet tools like Excel query data from a relational database using SQL improve data presentations using business intelligence tools like Tableau We will meet weekly, in-person, every Tuesday afternoon, September 15 - December 8, 2-3:30 PM (12 sessions). opportunities.description: Learn Python and build your programming skills in a supportive group. This learning circle will meet on Tuesday afternoons from September 22 to December 8, 2-3:30pm. Python Essentials 1 is the first in a 2-course series that teaches computer programming skills including how to design, develop, and improve computer programs using the Python programming language. opportunities.title: After School Club: Make a Kaleidoscope with Explorum
opportunities.description: What is a kaleidoscope? An optical illusion? Magic? Art? In fact, it's a bit of all that. It's an instrument developed over 200 years ago that uses the reflection of light on mirrors to create enchanting repetitive patterns. In this workshop, children will make their own kaleidoscope and are introduced to the terms reflection and refraction of light while being captivated by the physics of the shimmering patterns on reflective surfaces. Recommended materials: paper (thick card stock), scissors, aluminum foil, markers, glue stick, BBQ skewer, tape, (optional: sparkles) Zoom URL to access the online program will be emailed to registrants ahead of program date. This online program is suitable for children ages 6-12. Younger children may require assistance from caregivers. It is recommended that parents or caregivers are present during this live program. Questions about online programs? Please email us at programproposals@tpl.ca. opportunities.title: Tiny Titans: Insects Up Close | Book Launch & Panel Talk with Author & Photographer Dara Ojo
opportunities.description: Discover the hidden world of arthropods through stunning macro photography — a visual journey celebrating their beauty, complexity, and essential role in our ecosystems. Meet Dara Ojo , an award-winning macro photographer and conservation storyteller whose work brings the hidden world of arthropods into vivid relief. Ojo's book, Tiny Titans : The Silent Keepers of Our Ecosystem reveals the fascinating lives of insects, spiders, and other small creatures that quietly sustain life on Earth. Captured across Canada, Mexico, Costa Rica, and beyond, Dara Ojo’s photography highlights the intricate details and diversity of these often-overlooked species. Ojo will be leading the conversation with: Antonia Guidotti , a Collections Technician with a focus on Insects & Arachnids at the Royal Ontario Museum. Lorraine Johnson , author and native plant and ecological gardening advocate, bridging the connection between insects, plants, habitat and practical conservation action. Dr. Sandra Rehan , professor at York University and principal investigator of the Rehan Lab with a focus on wild bees, pollinator biology and conservation. Rehan's research explores the biology, behaviour and evolution of bees, with a particular interest in understanding and protecting native pollinators. Dr. Laura Timms , Senior Specialist of Natural Heritage Management at Credit Valley Conservation and Adjunct Professor with the Daniels Faculty’s Institute of Forestry and Conservation. Join in this evening to celebrate macro photography and the intricate beauty and ecological importance of insects and spiders, creatures that quietly anchor global biodiversity, pollination, and climate resilience. Free program. Register for a reminder. ***Doors open at 5:30 pm. At 6:00 pm, seating becomes first-come, first-served until capacity is reached.*** 5:30 pm: Doors open. Mingle and chat with fellow nature and environmental enthusiasts! 6:00 pm: Presentation begins. Enjoy a highly visual presentation combining photography, science, conservation and storytelling, taking the audience behind the scenes of six years documenting tiny worlds across five continents and exploring why these overlooked species matter. A light, informal conversation with guest speakers will explore why arthropods are so essential to our ecosystems, with a discussion of challenges impacting local species, and how science, photography and art can work together to help people notice, understand and care about the natural world. An audience Q&A follows this discussion. 7:30 pm: Book signing with books available for purchase. *** This program is part of TPL's Our Fragile Planet program series, supported by Friends of Toronto Public Library, South Chapter.​ Questions? Please contact North York Central Library - Business, Science & Technology Department. *** Place a hold or borrow from Toronto Public Library: Tiny Titans : The Silent Keepers of Our Ecosystem (book) - Dara Ojo A Garden for the Rusty-patched Bumblebee (book) - Lorraine Johnson *** Information Collection Notice: The personal information on this form is collected by the Toronto Public Library under the Public Libraries Act, sections 20(a), 20(c), and 20(d). The information will only be used for event and program registration, delivery and evaluation. Questions about how the library handles your information can be directed to Answerline staff at answerline@tpl.ca, 416-397-5981, 789 Yonge Street, Toronto ON M4W 2G8.

opportunities.title: Computers for Beginners
opportunities.description: Computers for Beginners 1: Use the Mouse A class on how to use a mouse for absolute beginners with little or no computer experience. In this first session you will: Observe and practice how to operate a mouse effectively Understand various mouse pointers and cursors Review basic keyboard functions Use the mouse for basic Windows functions Upon completion of this class students will be able to use a computer mouse at a basic level and will be able to go online for additional practice. Computers for Beginners 2: Use the Keyboard A class on basic keyboard functions for absolute beginners with little or no computer experience. In this second session you will: Familiarize yourself through practice with the most essential keyboard functions (alphabet, number and symbol keys) Practice proper keyboarding posture Upon completion of this class students will be able to use a keyboard at a beginner level and know how to go online for additional practice. Computers for Beginners 3: Use the Internet An introductory class on the Internet for absolute beginners with little computer experience. In this fourth session you will: Understand how to read a web site address Practice using web addresses Search for information using a search engine Explore a web site in detail to understand its key components Upon completion of this class students will be able to use the internet at a beginner level and complete simple searches. Computers for Beginners 4: Use Google Search and Maps A class on using Google's filters, tools, and Maps for absolute beginners with little computer experience. In this fifth session you will: Use Google search tools more effectively to find websites, images, and news sites Explore Google Maps to find addresses and get directions for transit and road travel. Upon completion of this class students will be able to use more advanced search engine features and use Google Maps at a basic level. Computers for Beginners 5: Use Windows A class on essential basic Windows skills for absolute beginners with little computer experience. In this third session you will: Become familiar with the Windows (10) operating system Practice using common Windows features: File Explorer, Desktop, Taskbar, Windows, Applications Upon completion of this class students will have a basic understanding of how to create and organize files in the Windows environment.

opportunities.title: Shedding light on the dark side of the Universe
opportunities.description: The standard model of cosmology tells us that the Universe is mostly made up of ‘Dark Matter’, with normal matter contributing only about 15% of the total budget. However, direct detections have not yielded any results about the nature of this mysterious dark matter, leaving us with only indirect means of inferring its existence and distribution. I will try to answer tantalizing questions about its nature, and how it may have helped shape the Universe. This talk will be given by Dr. Pratika Dayal from the Dunlap Institute for Astronomy & Astrophysics at the University of Toronto. No registration is required, but registering will make sure you receive a reminder. opportunities.title: AI for Us: Shaping AI in Toronto
opportunities.description: Toronto is one of the biggest AI cities in the world. But what do the people here actually think about it and how do we want to shape its development and use? A panel of experts, alongside our Innovator-in-Residence Ryan Kelln , who know AI from very different angles, unite for an open conversation about what AI is doing to this city, and what we want it to do instead. We'll talk about: The human beings behind the machines: what drives the people who build AI, and what worries them. Work, money, and meaning: what happens to jobs, creativity, and value when AI lands here. Who gets to shape it and who's left out (both are our neighbours). The stories we tell: how art, media, news, and everyday talk shape what we expect, fear, and hope for. No pitches, no boosterism. Just an honest conversation about the ideas and stories shaping AI in this city, and what we want it to become. Featuring: Jerrold McGrath , Cultural Programmer and Theorist, In the Meantime Joseph Wilson , Anthropologist & Author of Humans of AI: Understanding the Humans Behind the Machines Owais Lightwala , Assistant Professor, Performance at The Creative School at Toronto Metropolitan University, Director, Chrysalis Registration is required and will start November 9, 2026 at 12:30 PM. Note: Your spot will not be guaranteed after 5 minutes of the start of the program. After this time, remaining seats will be filled on a first come, first serve basis until capacity is reached. opportunities.title: Homeschoolers Weekly Meet-Up @ Angus Glen
opportunities.description: Are you a homeschooler family? Markham Public Library hosts weekly meetups for homeschooler families on Monday mornings at the Angus Glen Library Branch from 10:30AM - 12:00PM . These meetups give participating caregivers and children an opportunity to connect with other homeschooling families, work together to explore various STEAM building and literacy development focused activities, learn about library resources, meet special guest speakers, and more! PLEASE NOTE: Adults (caregivers) are responsible for supervising and assisting the children in their care with all planned activities and/or exercises Most planned activities are suitable for ages 5+ and may be subject to change Active participation and engagement of all caregivers is required ⚠️ PLEASE REGISTER TO ATTEND: We require advance registration for this program due to limited space, room capacity, and to support the library in our ability to plan activities and prepare supplies. We ask that all participants (caregivers and children) please sign-up for each session to guarantee your spot! *** ***For example, if there is 1 caregiver and 3 children attending, please indicate 4 in the registration.

opportunities.description: Ever wonder why stretching feels so good, or why one deep breath can change your whole mood? Wellness Unplugged is a laid-back workshop where teens can dig into the science and history behind yoga and Pilates. No experience, no equipment, no pressure. Come ready for honest conversations, journaling, and hands-on activities that give you real tools for everyday life. Hosted by the Villij, a Toronto-based wellness company rooted in mindful movement and community connection. Drop in. No registration required. This workshop is part of the Teen Social Health and Wellness programming. Generously supported by The Estate of Claudia Krawchuk. This program is part of Youth Hub service. Youth Hubs are a welcoming place for teens after school and in the summer, where helpful staff are always available. Free, nutritious snacks are offered daily. Drop by a branch with a Youth Hub or call the branch to find out more.

opportunities.title: Google Prompting Essentials: Online Learning Circle
opportunities.description: Ready to develop the skills to use generative AI (GenAI) tools effectively and responsibly for work and daily life? Join our staff-facilitated Learning Circle to complete the self-paced Google Prompting specialization. By completing this Learning Circle program, you will earn a Google Prompting Essentials certificate to share on your resume, LinkedIn and social media profiles! What You'll Learn This program is designed for those with some experience with using GenAI. Through short videos, articles, assignments and quizzes, you will discover: Essential Prompting Skills : How to use a prompting framework to create a desired output with GenAI; how to evaluate and refine your results. Everyday Work Tasks: Strategies to draft content, brainstorm ideas, create tables, timelines, and more. Data & Presentations: How to explore data visualization and use GenAI responsibly when working with data. Advanced Techniques: How to use prompt chaining for complex tasks and prompt versioning to save and reuse your best prompts over time. Learning Circles are study groups guided by library staff for people who want to complete the Google Prompting specialization together in a welcoming space: Learners meet weekly and work together through course materials. Participants are expected to commit to attending all four Learning Circle sessions. opportunities.title: From Interview Jitters to Interview Confidence: Navigating In-Person, Virtual and AI-Powered Interviews
opportunities.description: Interview formats are evolving, but the ability to communicate your experience, value and potential with confidence remains essential. This practical webinar will help job seekers prepare for in-person, virtual and increasingly common AI-powered interviews. Participants will learn how to manage interview anxiety, structure clear and compelling responses, communicate effectively on camera and adapt their approach to different interview formats. We will also explore what employers and recruiters assess during interviews, common mistakes to avoid, and how candidates can remain authentic and human throughout a technology-enabled hiring process. Attendees will leave with practical strategies to approach their next interview with greater clarity, preparation and confidence. Speaker Bio - Wagisha Singh is a Talent Acquisition Specialist with over six years of experience recruiting across Canada and the United States. She has partnered with organizations ranging from growing businesses to large national employers, hiring talent across logistics, transportation, supply chain, skilled trades, healthcare, accounting and finance, operations, and leadership roles. This program is part of TPL's Career Coaches in Residence and is generously supported by our lead donor Azrieli Foundation along with supporting donors Fidelity Canada, Friends of Toronto Public Library, South Chapter and The William and Nona Heaslip Foundation. For more information, please visit tpl.ca/careercoach

opportunities.title: Google Prompting Essentials: Online Learning Circle
opportunities.description: Ready to develop the skills to use generative AI (GenAI) tools effectively and responsibly for work and daily life? Join our staff-facilitated Learning Circle to complete the self-paced Google Prompting specialization. By completing this Learning Circle program, you will earn a Google Prompting Essentials certificate to share on your resume, LinkedIn and social media profiles! What You'll Learn This program is designed for those with some experience with using GenAI. Through short videos, articles, assignments and quizzes, you will discover: Essential Prompting Skills : How to use a prompting framework to create a desired output with GenAI; how to evaluate and refine your results. Everyday Work Tasks: Strategies to draft content, brainstorm ideas, create tables, timelines, and more. Data & Presentations: How to explore data visualization and use GenAI responsibly when working with data. Advanced Techniques: How to use prompt chaining for complex tasks and prompt versioning to save and reuse your best prompts over time. Learning Circles are study groups guided by library staff for people who want to complete the Google Prompting specialization together in a welcoming space: Learners meet weekly and work together through course materials. Participants are expected to commit to attending all four Learning Circle sessions. Some Experience with GenAI Recommended: This course is ideal for participants who have completed the AI Essentials course Learning Circle. How to Joi n a Learning Circle: Register once for the first session of this event series, in order to attend all sessions. Please sign up with a valid email address. A valid TPL library card is required for online circles. Attend all four sessions online via Zoom, on Tuesdays December 1, 8, 15 from 1:30-4:30pm. Registration is a two-step process. opportunities.title: Peek Inside an AI Assistant: How It Thinks and Works
opportunities.description: You've asked an AI chatbot questions. But there's another kind of AI that doesn't just answer: it acts. In this demo-driven talk with our Innovator-in-Residence, Ryan Kelln , we'll look deeply at always-on personal AI assistants. The assistant can read your files, use your apps, and remember what you've told it, growing more useful over time. The same powers that let it help you can hurt you if something goes wrong. We'll also open up what happens inside: the hidden instructions, the tools it uses, what it remembers and forgets. Then we'll look at the AI assistant that helped develop this workshop, and how we shaped our workflow together, and why. Registration is required and will start November 9, 2026 at 12:30 PM. Note: Your spot will not be guaranteed after 5 minutes of the start of the program. After this time, remaining seats will be filled on a first come, first serve basis until capacity is reached. opportunities.title: Sven Beckert: A Global History of Capitalism
opportunities.description: TPL and Toronto Metropolitan University present historian Sven Beckert in conversation with Sanjay Ruparelia at the Toronto Reference Library's Appel Salon. As the Laird Bell Professor of History at Harvard University and co-chair of the university's Program on the Study of Capitalism, Sven Beckert has spent his career tracing how a single economic system came to structure nearly every aspect of modern life, how we work, how we think about ourselves and others, and how we organize our politics. In Capitalism: A Global History , Beckert reveals that capitalism was born global, corresponding at no point to an idealized dream of free markets; from the outset, state-backed institutions, imperial expansion, and coercion shaped its dynamics as much as innovation and exchange did. Along the way, capitalism has both expanded political voice for some and violently foreclosed it for others, entangled from its origins with slavery, colonialism, and profound inequality. How do we distinguish between capitalism's capacity to generate genuine prosperity and its tendency to concentrate power in ways that undermine democratic institutions? What can nearly a thousand years of capitalist history teach us about the conditions under which economic systems support, rather than erode, democratic life? And as we confront what many call a crisis of late-stage capitalism, what possibilities remain for reimagining an economic order more compatible with democratic values? Join one of the world's foremost historians of capitalism for an essential conversation about the deep entanglement of markets and democracy, and what history suggests about the road ahead. Question and answer session and book signing to follow. Books available for purchase. About this Event's Guests: Sven Beckert Sanjay Ruparelia Read More: Capitalism Empire of Cotton *** This event is part of our On Civil Society series, where we host local and international authors, activists and academics in conversation about the most critical topics of our time. Generously supported by the McConnell Foundation and also by Chris M. Reid. *** About the series: On the Frontlines of Democracy is a public lecture series to analyze the trajectory of democracy in the twenty-first century. In every region, the prospects of democracy face serious challenges, old and new. Can we protect constitutional rights and renew collective self-rule in an era of popular mistrust, severe partisanship and resurgent nationalism? Can they reduce inequalities of power, wealth and status, defend deep diversity and confront climate change in the new digital age? Can we develop innovative strategies to revitalize civic engagement, empower public institutions and resist autocratic threats? And what can we offer, learn and do to promote the prospects of democracy in our increasingly post-western global order? *** PLAN YOUR VISIT : Location: Bram and Bluma Appel Salon, Toronto Reference Library (789 Yonge Street), 2nd floor Time: Doors open 6:00 pm, Event starts 7 pm. Tickets: Free registration required. Ticket policy: Tickets guaranteed until 6:50 pm, after which rush line admission begins. Seating first come, first served. Bar: Beer/wine available for purchase (debit/credit only). TPL is committed to accessibility. If you are Deaf or have a disability and would like to request accommodation for this event, please contact accessibleservices@tpl.ca or 416-393-7099 at least three weeks prior to the event. *** Information Collection Notice: The personal information on this form is collected by the Toronto Public Library under the Public Libraries Act, sections 20(a), 20(c), and 20(d). opportunities.title: AI At Home: No Cloud, No Account
opportunities.description: What if your AI didn't need the internet at all: no subscription, no one recording what you type? In this class led by our Innovator-in-Residence, Ryan Kelln , you'll see AI models running entirely on one computer, with no connection and no data leaving the room. We'll compare a small local model against a powerful cloud model and plain search: what each gets right, what each costs, and what the privacy trade-offs really are. You'll leave with a decision sheet for your own hardware, an installation recipe, and an honest look at what "open" really means when it comes to AI. opportunities.description: How does a machine actually "think"? Explore the history and latest developments of machine learning. opportunities.title: AI, Our Community and What Happens Next
opportunities.description: Twelve weeks of making, testing, and learning. Now what do we do with it? Join Innovator in Residence Ryan Kelln for his closing event, as he reflects on the Applied AI residency: the projects people built, the unexpected moments that taught us the most, and the needs we discovered but couldn't solve. We'll tell our stories. Then it's your turn. In small groups, we'll ask: what should we continue, what should we change? opportunities.title: Youth Hub: Walking, Swimming, Flying - Hands-On Nature
opportunities.description: Explore the different ways organisms move (and moved) around on Planet Earth. Some walk, some swim, and others fly. Can you tell which is which? Participants will be able to handle, study and learn about strange objects: fossils, replicas and modern specimens. They will be guides all through the how, when and why these organisms adapted to move as they do. Interactive, entertaining and educational, join us for a journey in living locomotion. This program is part of Youth Hub service. Youth Hubs are a welcoming place for teens after school and in the summer, where helpful staff are always available. Free, nutritious snacks are offered daily. Drop by a branch with a Youth Hub or call the branch to find out more.

No previous experience with these tools is necessary. Please bring a smartphone. Participants will practice: Adding appointments and events to a calendar. Setting reminders, alarms and timers. opportunities.description: Are you a homeschooler family? Markham Public Library hosts weekly meetups for homeschooler families on Monday mornings at the Angus Glen Library Branch from 10:30AM - 12:00PM . These meetups give participating caregivers and children an opportunity to connect with other homeschooling families, work together to explore various STEAM building and literacy development focused activities, learn about library resources, meet special guest speakers, and more! PLEASE NOTE: Adults (caregivers) are responsible for supervising and assisting the children in their care with all planned activities and/or exercises Most planned activities are suitable for ages 5+ and may be subject to change Active participation and engagement of all caregivers is required ⚠️ PLEASE REGISTER TO ATTEND: We require advance registration for this program due to limited space, room capacity, and to support the library in our ability to plan activities and prepare supplies. We ask that all participants (caregivers and children) please sign-up for each session to guarantee your spot! *** ***For example, if there is 1 caregiver and 3 children attending, please indicate 4 in the registration.

opportunities.description: Step into a fun, hands-on financial literacy experience where children learn, spend, make decisions, and put their money skills to the test through an interactive simulation workshop. Inspired by I'm a Kid with a Mortgage! , this engaging workshop is presented by Robert Coutts, the author of I'm a Kid with a Mortgage!, and an Ontario Elementary school teacher. This high-energy workshop combines storytelling, games, group activities, and a financial simulation designed for students in Grades 3–7. Participants will receive a copy of I'm a Kid with a Mortgage! and a digital Activity & Colouring Book following the program. Learning Outcomes Explore key financial literacy concepts such as earning, spending, saving, budgeting, and making informed financial decisions. Develop creative thinking and entrepreneurship skills through interactive activities and real-world scenarios.

This interactive workshop includes hands-on activities, resource sharing, discussion, and practical classroom applications (which can also apply to parents at home too). Participants will receive a copy of I'm a Kid with a Mortgage! , a digital Activity & Coloring Book, and a digital 15-Day Financial Literacy Unit. Note:Coffee, snacks, and light refreshments will be provided. Learning Outcomes Explore strategies for teaching budgeting, saving, earning, borrowing, entrepreneurship, and financial decision-making in an engaging and age-appropriate way. opportunities.description: Are you interested in Waterloo math contests but unsure where to start? Or are you looking for ways to prepare more effectively? Whether you are a first-time participant or have competed before, you will learn practical strategies to guide your preparation. In this workshop, you will learn about: Choosing a Waterloo math contest suited to your grade and experience (Euclid, Fermat, Hypatia, Cayley, Galois) Creating a manageable study plan and using past contest questions Connecting classroom math with contest problem-solving Managing your time and deciding which questions to attempt first Free preparation materials will be provided, with time for questions. This program is suitable for high school students and no previous contest experience is required. ** Please note: If you are interested in joining us for part 2 of the Waterloo Math Contests preparation class, please join us on Sat. opportunities.description: Online shopping gives us convenience and more choices, but it also means dealing with more products, reviews, advertisements and recommendations. In this session, Dan, who brings a background in computer programming and IT support, will lead to explore how digital tools are changing the way people shop and discuss how we can make more informed choices online. Topics may include comparing information, understanding reviews and recommendations, and common questions around trust and online shopping safety. Participants are welcome to bring shopping questions or examples they have encountered online for discussion. 網上購物為我們帶來方便及更多選擇，但同時亦要面對大量產品資料、評論、廣告及推薦內容。 本次數碼探索小組會一起探討科技如何改變我們的購物方式，以及如何更有意識地使用網上資訊作出選擇。討論可能涉及產品比較、網上評論、推薦內容、廣告，以及網上購物時常見的可信程度和安全問題。 本次探索小組由擁有電腦編程及IT支援經驗的Dan老師主講，一起交流和討論為主，歡迎參加者分享自己網上購物時遇到的問題、經驗或有趣例子，一起研究及討論。 建議參加者具備基本智能手機操作經驗。 以粵語及國語進行。 請自備智能手機出席。

opportunities.title: Fact, Fiction, or AI? Finding Reliable Health Information Online
opportunities.description: Presented in partnership with North York General Hospital's Health Resource Centre for Patients and Families : We are living in a remarkable era for health information. More information than ever is available at our fingertips, and artificial intelligence is rapidly changing how we find, understand, and use it. These large language models are packed with helpful knowledge and useful insight. And we wouldn’t want to miss out on these benefits. But more information does not always mean better information. Search engines, social media, websites, and AI tools can make it difficult to distinguish reliable health information from misinformation, outdated advice, or remarkably convincing errors. Even sophisticated AI systems can produce information that sounds authoritative but is wrong. This interactive session will explore both the opportunities and the pitfalls of navigating information online - including using AI for health information. Participants will be exposed to tips, tools, and techniques for safer and more effective searching. They will also gain more appreciation for how easily we can be led astray. We will explore how AI tools respond to different inputs, and learn the best ways to engineer our prompts. We will also explore practical strategies for checking information using the SIFT method and discuss situations where information should always be independently verified. The session will conclude with a practical list of reliable health resources, including human sources of help! By the end of the session, participants will leave with new skills for critical thinking, safer and more effective use of AI, and a toolkit of trusted health resources, including reliable sources of human support.

opportunities.title: Waterloo Math Contests: Tips for Success — Problem-Solving Practice (Grades 10-12)
opportunities.description: What can you do when a math contest question looks unfamiliar? How can you turn your ideas into a clear solution? Join Hope Zhang, a high school Math teacher at Ace Acumen Heights, for a free, interactive workshop exploring Waterloo math contest questions. Through guided practice and discussion, students will try to break challenging problems into manageable steps. In this workshop, you will practise: Identifying key information and choosing a starting point Applying algebra, geometry, and logical reasoning Comparing different approaches to the same problem Check the question from past test to be familiar with difficulty of the contest Free practice materials will be provided, with time to ask questions and share ideas. Suitable for high school students. Students are welcome to attend whether or not they joined the first workshop. Please bring a pencil and paper.

opportunities.description: Are you a homeschooler family? Markham Public Library hosts weekly meetups for homeschooler families on Monday mornings at the Angus Glen Library Branch from 10:30AM - 12:00PM . These meetups give participating caregivers and children an opportunity to connect with other homeschooling families, work together to explore various STEAM building and literacy development focused activities, learn about library resources, meet special guest speakers, and more! PLEASE NOTE: Adults (caregivers) are responsible for supervising and assisting the children in their care with all planned activities and/or exercises Most planned activities are suitable for ages 5+ and may be subject to change Active participation and engagement of all caregivers is required ⚠️ PLEASE REGISTER TO ATTEND: We require advance registration for this program due to limited space, room capacity, and to support the library in our ability to plan activities and prepare supplies. We ask that all participants (caregivers and children) please sign-up for each session to guarantee your spot! *** ***For example, if there is 1 caregiver and 3 children attending, please indicate 4 in the registration.

opportunities.title: Digital Discovery Club: Social Media Literacy (Mandarin & Cantonese) 數碼探索小組：社交媒體
opportunities.description: Why do certain posts keep appearing on our screens? Why does some information spread so quickly? And how can we decide what deserves our attention or trust? This discussion-based session led by Dan, who brings a background in computer programming and IT support, will explore how we experience information on social media, including recommendations, sharing, privacy and misleading content. The goal is not to learn one particular social media platform, but to become more thoughtful and confident when viewing and sharing information online. Participants are encouraged to bring questions, observations or examples they have encountered for the group to discuss. 為甚麼某些帖文會不斷出現在我們的手機？為甚麼有些消息可以在短時間內傳遍社交媒體？我們又可以如何判斷哪些內容值得相信或分享？ 本次數碼探索小組由擁有電腦編程及IT支援經驗的Dan老師從日常使用社交媒體的經驗出發，一起討論推薦內容、資訊分享、私隱及誤導資訊等議題。重點並不是教授某一個社交媒體平台的操作，而是幫助參加者更有意識及更有信心地理解網上看到的資訊。 歡迎參加者帶來自己曾經看過的內容、遇到的問題或觀察，一起交流及討論。 建議參加者具備基本智能手機操作經驗。 以粵語及國語進行。 請自備智能手機出席

opportunities.title: Teaching Financial Literacy Through Real-World Experiences
opportunities.description: Looking for ways to teach financial literacy to your students or children? Discover practical ways to bring financial literacy concepts into your space through interactive activities, real-world examples, and teaching strategies inspired by I'm a Kid with a Mortgage! . Led by Robert Coutts, author of I'm a Kid with a Mortgage! and an Ontario Elementary teacher , this workshop will equip you with resources and ideas to help students build money-management skills and confidence. This interactive workshop includes hands-on activities, resource sharing, discussion, and practical classroom applications (which can also apply to parents at home too). Participants will receive a copy of I'm a Kid with a Mortgage! , a digital Activity & Coloring Book, and a digital 15-Day Financial Literacy Unit. Note:Coffee, snacks, and light refreshments will be provided. Learning Outcomes Explore strategies for teaching budgeting, saving, earning, borrowing, entrepreneurship, and financial decision-making in an engaging and age-appropriate way. Gain ready-to-use activities, classroom resources, and practical tools to support financial literacy learning.

opportunities.description: Are you a homeschooler family? Markham Public Library hosts weekly meetups for homeschooler families on Monday mornings at the Angus Glen Library Branch from 10:30AM - 12:00PM . These meetups give participating caregivers and children an opportunity to connect with other homeschooling families, work together to explore various STEAM building and literacy development focused activities, learn about library resources, meet special guest speakers, and more! PLEASE NOTE: Adults (caregivers) are responsible for supervising and assisting the children in their care with all planned activities and/or exercises Most planned activities are suitable for ages 5+ and may be subject to change Active participation and engagement of all caregivers is required ⚠️ PLEASE REGISTER TO ATTEND: We require advance registration for this program due to limited space, room capacity, and to support the library in our ability to plan activities and prepare supplies. Markham Public Library hosts weekly meetups for homeschooler families on Monday mornings at the Angus Glen Library Branch from 10:30AM - 12:00PM . PLEASE NOTE: Adults (caregivers) are responsible for supervising and assisting the children in their care with all planned activities and/or exercises Most planned activities are suitable for ages 5+ and may be subject to change Active participation and engagement of all caregivers is required ⚠️ PLEASE REGISTER TO ATTEND: We require advance registration for this program due to limited space, room capacity, and to support the library in our ability to plan activities and prepare supplies. opportunities.title: STEM in Action - Engineering Activities
opportunities.description: Mechanical Engineer: Egg Drop Challenge Can you design a system that keeps an egg safe from a big drop? In this hands-on engineering challenge, participants will design, build, and test a protective structure using provided materials to cushion an egg from impact. As they experiment with different designs, they'll explore key engineering concepts such as forces, impact absorption, and structural design while learning how engineers solve real-world problems. Through testing, redesigning, and improving their prototypes, participants will develop creativity, critical thinking, and problem-solving skills while putting their engineering ideas to the test. Participants: Children aged 8 - 13 years old Note: Please sign up for each of the four sessions for your child(ren) to be able to attend all four unique sessions in this program series.

opportunities.title: Homeschoolers Weekly Meet-Up @ Angus Glen
opportunities.description: Are you a homeschooler family? Markham Public Library hosts weekly meetups for homeschooler families on Monday mornings at the Angus Glen Library Branch from 10:30AM - 12:00PM . These meetups give participating caregivers and children an opportunity to connect with other homeschooling families, work together to explore various STEAM building and literacy development focused activities, learn about library resources, meet special guest speakers, and more! PLEASE NOTE: Adults (caregivers) are responsible for supervising and assisting the children in their care with all planned activities and/or exercises Most planned activities are suitable for ages 5+ and may be subject to change Active participation and engagement of all caregivers is required ⚠️ PLEASE REGISTER TO ATTEND: We require advance registration for this program due to limited space, room capacity, and to support the library in our ability to plan activities and prepare supplies. We ask that all participants (caregivers and children) please sign-up for each session to guarantee your spot! *** ***For example, if there is 1 caregiver and 3 children attending, please indicate 4 in the registration.

Markham Public Library hosts weekly meetups for homeschooler families on Monday mornings at the Angus Glen Library Branch from 10:30AM - 12:00PM . PLEASE NOTE: Adults (caregivers) are responsible for supervising and assisting the children in their care with all planned activities and/or exercises Most planned activities are suitable for ages 5+ and may be subject to change Active participation and engagement of all caregivers is required ⚠️ PLEASE REGISTER TO ATTEND: We require advance registration for this program due to limited space, room capacity, and to support the library in our ability to plan activities and prepare supplies. opportunities.title: Resilience Reads: a climate neighbourhood reading party
opportunities.description: Join us to share the joy of reading, while building climate resilience knowledge. Members are invited to discuss a book they are reading, tell stories, and empower each other to explore community-driven solutions. Each party will start with a quiet read and reflect time, with opportunities to join group discussions later on over refreshments. AUGUST – Fossil Fuel Folly American War by Omar El Akkad or your favourite dystopian read! or your favourite book featuring water! SEPTEMBER – We Need Pollinators The History of Bees by Maja Lunde or your favourite animal-centred book! OCTOBER – Climate Change is Scary The Annual Migration of Clouds by Premee Mohamed or a different book that shares a scary future ecological crisis! NOVEMBER - Climate Changes Everything Ministry for the Future by Kim Stanley Robinson or your favourite time travel read! Copies are available in the branch to pick up, while supplies last. Registration is encouraged but drop ins are welcome! opportunities.title: Homeschoolers Weekly Meet-Up @ Angus Glen
opportunities.description: Are you a homeschooler family? Markham Public Library hosts weekly meetups for homeschooler families on Monday mornings at the Angus Glen Library Branch from 10:30AM - 12:00PM . These meetups give participating caregivers and children an opportunity to connect with other homeschooling families, work together to explore various STEAM building and literacy development focused activities, learn about library resources, meet special guest speakers, and more! PLEASE NOTE: Adults (caregivers) are responsible for supervising and assisting the children in their care with all planned activities and/or exercises Most planned activities are suitable for ages 5+ and may be subject to change Active participation and engagement of all caregivers is required ⚠️ PLEASE REGISTER TO ATTEND: We require advance registration for this program due to limited space, room capacity, and to support the library in our ability to plan activities and prepare supplies. We ask that all participants (caregivers and children) please sign-up for each session to guarantee your spot! *** ***For example, if there is 1 caregiver and 3 children attending, please indicate 4 in the registration.

opportunities.description: Are you a homeschooler family? Markham Public Library hosts weekly meetups for homeschooler families on Monday mornings at the Angus Glen Library Branch from 10:30AM - 12:00PM . These meetups give participating caregivers and children an opportunity to connect with other homeschooling families, work together to explore various STEAM building and literacy development focused activities, learn about library resources, meet special guest speakers, and more! PLEASE NOTE: Adults (caregivers) are responsible for supervising and assisting the children in their care with all planned activities and/or exercises Most planned activities are suitable for ages 5+ and may be subject to change Active participation and engagement of all caregivers is required ⚠️ PLEASE REGISTER TO ATTEND: We require advance registration for this program due to limited space, room capacity, and to support the library in our ability to plan activities and prepare supplies. We ask that all participants (caregivers and children) please sign-up for each session to guarantee your spot! *** ***For example, if there is 1 caregiver and 3 children attending, please indicate 4 in the registration.
